name: John James Piatt
credit: Photograph of John James Piatt, c. 1900 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: John James Piatt (1835–1917) was an American poet born in Indiana and raised in Ohio. With William Dean Howells he published Poems of Two Friends (1860), and he worked as a journalist and government clerk in Washington before serving as United States consul at Cork, Ireland.
He was married to the poet Sarah Morgan Bryan Piatt, and several of their volumes of verse appeared under both names.

poems.title: Apart
poems.author: John James Piatt
poems.collection: The Golden Treasury of American Songs and Lyrics (1899)
poems.text:
At sea are tossing ships;
  On shore are dreaming shells,
And the waiting heart and the loving lips,
  Blossoms and bridal bells.

At sea are sails a-gleam;
  On shore are longing eyes,
And the far horizon's haunting dream
  Of ships that sail the skies.

At sea are masts that rise
  Like spectres from the deep;
On shore are the ghosts of drowning cries
  That cross the waves of sleep.

At sea are wrecks a-strand;
  On shore are shells that moan,
Old anchors buried in barren sand,
  Sea-mist and dreams alone.
